page: Microsoft Azure NC72lds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine designed for compute-heavy graphics, rendering, and artificial intelligence workloads that require fractional GPU capabilities. Powered by an Intel x86_64 processor architecture running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provisions 72 dedicated vCPUs accompanied by 132.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a lean memory profile of approximately 1.83 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is supplied via a partitioned NVIDIA Blackwell architecture RTX PRO 6000 GPU, configured as a 0.5 fractional GPU unit with 48 GB of allocated VRAM. Complementing the compute and accelerator resources, the virtual server includes 3986 GB of local NVMe SSD storage to accommodate high-throughput scratch and caching operations, while also supporting external Azure Premium Storage volumes. Complimentary public IPv4 networking is not included with this instance.

The architectural design couples high dedicated core density with a partitioned enterprise workstation GPU, providing qualitative cost efficiency for organizations that require significant graphics memory without bearing the overhead of an entire physical GPU. Primary workload fits include 3D visual rendering, engineering simulation, computer-aided design (CAD), video post-processing pipelines, and intermediate machine learning inference models requiring low-latency local NVMe scratch space.

It fits compute-heavy tasks such as CAD rendering, video production, engineering simulation, and medium-scale model inference.
